correctness.rationale: For K_{n,n} with exactly (n,n) missing, parity gives the standard weighted-square identity. Two explicitly justified Cauchy–Schwarz RMS symmetrizations, column then row, do not decrease E Q⁴ at fixed energy and reduce to three block magnitudes t,u,v. With k=n−1 and mass fractions p,q,r, direct symbolic substitution independently verifies the exact quadratic deficit C_n−F=(6k²+k−4)(p−p*)²/k²+(q−r)²/k for p+q+r=1, with p*=k(6k−5)/(6k²+k−4); q=r=(3k−2)/(6k²+k−4). Thus global sharp C_n, unique positive two-level magnitudes. Every cycle of the punctured complete bipartite graph splits by an available chord into rectangles (n=2 is a tree), so positive rectangle sign products are exactly row/column sign switchings. Independent exact symbolic full-square deficit tends to 6/n² and checks C2,C3,C4; finite source diagnostics are not the all-n proof.
risks: Real independent signs only; not a complex coefficient, multiple-hole, or all-graph stability theorem.
The quadratic deficit is proved only on the symmetrized three-block class; no claim it controls all arbitrary arrays directly.

originality.rationale: Exact one-corner deletion of full bilinear chaos is not the full tensor product covered by scalar Khintchine: the latter only yields a strictly larger constant. The 1999 bilinear-form moment literature studies complete/unweighted and distribution-variable moment inequalities and missing diagonal patterns, not arbitrary real weighted one-corner coefficient arrays or complete sign-switching extremizers. Resultary found the assigned finding, no dominating puncture theorem. Novelty remains best of knowledge.
